5491.correction: Phone cameras are powerful, but professional cameras give more control, lens options, and depth of field, which matters for creative and technical work.

933.belief: Changing the aperture or shutter speed only affects how bright the photo is.
933.statement: Changing the aperture or shutter speed only affects how bright the photo is.
933.correction: While both aperture and shutter speed do affect exposure (how light or dark a photo is), they also have creative effects on how the photo looks, such as blur.

4154.belief: Lighting is just a technical tool in photography.
4154.statement: Lighting is just a technical tool in photography.
4154.correction: Lighting has the power to transform a photograph, shaping its mood, tone, and clarity.

2250.belief: Depth of field is only controled by moving the camera nearer or further away from the subject.
2250.statement: Depth of field is only controled by moving the camera nearer or further away from the subject.
2250.correction: Depth of field is mainly controlled by adjusting the aperture (f-stop).

5494.belief: Photographers can't control the way movement is depicted in their photographs.
5494.statement: Photographers can't control the way movement is depicted in their photographs.
5494.correction: Photographers can freeze action sharply or blur it creatively, depending on the photographer’s intent.

9056.belief: The safelight allows any kind of light to be on in the darkroom without damaging prints.
9056.statement: The safelight allows any kind of light to be on in the darkroom without damaging prints.
9056.correction: The safelight is not a “free pass” for unlimited light exposure and that all light exposure must be controlled and time-sensitive.

5492.belief: Photo editing is always obvious or “fake”.
5492.statement: Photo editing is always obvious or “fake”.
5492.correction: In reality, edits can be extremely subtle and still have a significant impact on the final image.

2586.belief: Editing an image always changes or damages the original file.
2586.statement: Editing an image always changes or damages the original file.
2586.correction: By using adjustment layers and layer masks, edits are non-destructive.

8910.belief: Research is separate from making work.
8910.statement: Research is separate from making work.
8910.correction: Research feeds directly into experimentation and outcomes.

9141.belief: Sculpture must be realistic or life-like to be considered good.
9141.statement: Sculpture must be realistic or life-like to be considered good.
9141.correction: Sculpture can be abstract or symbolic, focusing on space, balance, and movement rather than realism.

2855.belief: Expensive or traditional materials are better for making sculptures.
2855.statement: Expensive or traditional materials are better for making sculptures.
2855.correction: Any material can be powerful in sculpture if it supports the concept or message being expressed.

10066.belief: Surface texture is just decoration and doesn’t really matter.
10066.statement: Surface texture is just decoration and doesn’t really matter.
10066.correction: Surface texture plays a key role in communicating meaning, mood, or identity in sculpture.

3140.belief: Found materials are just junk and don’t belong in real artwork.
3140.statement: Found materials are just junk and don’t belong in real artwork.
3140.correction: Found materials bring unique textures and personal or cultural meaning to a sculpture.

555.belief: Basic clay techniques like pinch or coil are only for beginners.
555.statement: Basic clay techniques like pinch or coil are only for beginners.
555.correction: Simple clay techniques can be used to build complex and expressive sculptural forms.

10064.belief: Surface decoration should be added at the end and doesn’t need much thought.
10064.statement: Surface decoration should be added at the end and doesn’t need much thought.
10064.correction: Surface design should be planned and integrated to reflect and enhance the sculptural idea.

5745.belief: I can just pour all the plaster at once and it will work.
5745.statement: I can just pour all the plaster at once and it will work.
5745.correction: Plaster heats as it sets and pouring too much at once can trap air, cause cracks or damage the model. Layering ensures detail and structure.

864.belief: Cardboard is too weak to build strong structures.
864.statement: Cardboard is too weak to build strong structures.
864.correction: Cardboard becomes structurally strong when layered, folded or rolled. It is even used in architecture and furniture design for its surprising durability.

422.belief: All artists make art about their intenral and external influences.
422.statement: All artists make art about their intenral and external influences.
422.correction: Some artists make art that is obviously about their influences and some don't.

4388.belief: Making mistakes in art is always bad for your artistic development.
4388.statement: Making mistakes in art is always bad for your artistic development.
4388.correction: Mistakes and experimentation can lead to developing an artistic voice.

9360.belief: Sketchbooks capture final outcomes and perfect work.
9360.statement: Sketchbooks capture final outcomes and perfect work
9360.correction: Sketchbooks capture not only the final outcomes but also the processes and innovations behind more finished works.

10226.belief: Themes in art are interpreted in the same way by all artists.
10226.statement: Themes in art are interpreted in the same way by all artists
10226.correction: Themes in art can inspire creativity while allowing for individual interpretation.

409.belief: Artist research is about making your work like another artist's artwork.
409.statement: Artist research is about making your work like another artist's artwork.
409.correction: Recording and analysing an artist’s work is essential for developing your understanding of techniques, concepts, and creative processes. We don't need to copy an artist's work but can take and apply knowledge and ideas inspired by relevant artists.

419.belief: Artists jump straight from inspiration to a finished artwork.
419.statement: Artists jump straight from inspiration to a finished artwork.
419.correction: Artists spend significant time experimenting, revising, and refining their ideas before arriving at a final piece.

2988.belief: A final piece represents the culmination of an artist's whole life's work, all their ideas and all the materials they have ever used.
2988.statement: A final piece represents the culmination of an artist's whole life's work, all their ideas and all the materials they have ever used.
2988.correction: A final piece represents the culmination of an artist's themes, materials and techniques, and artistic voice, at a particular moment in time.

10549.belief: Unlike artists, a graphic designer's personal experiences and preferences have no influence on their work and style.
10549.statement: Unlike artists, a graphic designer's personal experiences and preferences have no influence on their work and style.
10549.correction: The designer’s individual experiences, interests, and aesthetic preferences play a role in shaping a designer's unique style.

3378.belief: Graphic desingers only use digtial tools.
3378.statement: Graphic desingers only use digtial tools.
3378.correction: Traditional approaches to graphic design existed before digital tools and are still widely used today.

438.correction: Both artists and graphic designers use sketchbooks for creative exploration. The way they use them may differ in purpose, content, and process.

2300.belief: Designing in response to a theme means drawing something direct or literal.
2300.statement: Designing in response to a theme means drawing something direct or literal.
2300.correction: Themes are open to interpretation - good design often uses symbolism, abstraction and personal meaning to create deeper, more thoughtful responses.

8909.belief: A research page is just a collection of pictures and facts.
8909.statement: A research page is just a collection of pictures and facts.
8909.correction: Research pages are not about collecting facts - they’re about showing how you understand and respond to a designer’s work through layout, analysis, and visual interpretation.

2278.belief: A design concept is just choosing what looks good.
2278.statement: A design concept is just choosing what looks good.
2278.correction: A strong design concept isn’t just about appearance - it reflects a deeper idea or message you want to communicate. What you choose to show should connect to your personal voice and purpose.

2986.belief: The final piece should just copy the designer’s style.
2986.statement: The final piece should just copy the designer’s style.
2986.correction: While your chosen designer should influence your work, the final piece should show your own creative voice. Think about what you want to communicate, and how the designer’s style can help you do that - not just replicate it.

5496.belief: A photographic voice stays the same for the whole of the photographer’s lifetime.
5496.statement: A photographic voice stays the same for the whole of the photographer’s lifetime.
5496.correction: A photographic voice is not fixed. It can change, like we do.

4153.correction: Lighting plays a crucial role in setting the mood and atmosphere of a photograph.

5498.belief: Photography journals are always in book form.
5498.statement: Photography journals are always in book form.
5498.correction: They can also exist digitally or as collections of images, notes, and sketches in various formats.

10227.belief: Themes in photography are interpreted in the same way by all photographers.
10227.statement: Themes in photography are interpreted in the same way by all photographers.
10227.correction: Themes in photography can inspire creativity while allowing for individual interpretation.

4294.belief: Looking at other photographers’ work doesn’t help you to create your own ideas.
4294.statement: Looking at other photographers’ work doesn’t help you to create your own ideas.
4294.correction: Studying other photographers doesn’t mean copying. It helps you learn new techniques, discover styles you like and shape your own original ideas with more confidence.

1909.belief: A concept has to be something complex or deep to be valid.
1909.statement: A concept has to be something complex or deep to be valid.
1909.correction: Strong concepts can be simple but meaningful. The key is personal connection and clarity of intent.

10122.belief: You can just take random photos and pick the best ones later.
10122.statement: You can just take random photos and pick the best ones later.
10122.correction: Intentional planning makes each photo stronger and ensures the series works as a whole - not just as individual images.

9997.belief: Style is something that you have to figure out immediately.
9997.statement: Style is something that you have to figure out immediately.
9997.correction: Your textile style will grow and change as you explore materials, artists and your own ideas. You don’t have to know it yet.

2856.belief: Experimentation is only about making something perfect or a finished product.
2856.statement: Experimentation is only about making something perfect or a finished product.
2856.correction: Experimentation is about exploring and learning through trial and error. Showing how you develop your ideas is key to finding your textile voice.

10038.belief: A successful sketchbook has to be neat and tidy.
10038.statement: A successful sketchbook has to be neat and tidy.
10038.correction: A creative sketchbook values risk-taking, layering and visible thinking — not just clean layouts.

10222.belief: A theme limits creativity because you have to stick to one idea.
10222.statement: A theme limits creativity because you have to stick to one idea.
10222.correction: Themes are broad starting points, allowing many creative directions and personal interpretations.

10206.belief: Textile artist research pages have to be decorative to be good.
10206.statement: Textile artist research pages have to be decorative to be good.
10206.correction: A strong research page is not about decoration — it's about clear organisation, relevant visual responses and thoughtful annotations that show understanding of the artist’s work.

11199.belief: Your textile concept has to look like your artist’s work.
11199.statement: Your textile concept has to look like your artist’s work.
11199.correction: A strong artist response adapts inspiration to create something new and personal.

2985.belief: A final piece has to be big or completely different from my previous work.
2985.statement: A final piece has to be big or completely different from my previous work.
2985.correction: A strong final piece develops from your earlier ideas. It doesn’t need to be large or totally new — thoughtful refinement, consistent concept and clear links to your research and samples are what matter most.

2295.belief: A designer's style is fixed and remains constant.
2295.statement: A designer's style is fixed and remains constant.
2295.correction: A designer will grow and develop and so their distinctive style will evolve over time as they experiment more and engage with new ideas.

2857.belief: Experimentation just means making new things each time.
2857.statement: Experimentation just means making new things each time.
2857.correction: When you experiment you are thinking and doing. Always think about what works and what new ideas are generated.

9362.belief: Sketchbooks have a set format, and must be presented in the 'right' way.
9362.statement: Sketchbooks have a set format, and must be presented in the 'right' way.
9362.correction: Sketchbooks are a personal record of your own creative journey, but in the GCSE course they also allow you to gain marks, so sometimes we recommend working in a certain way to help you achieve.

5059.belief: It should be obvious how to explore a theme and reponses will be similar.
5059.statement: It should be obvious how to explore a theme and reponses will be similar.
5059.correction: Every person brings their own experiences to a theme so which aspect and how you explore it will depend on you, your background and your unique artistic voice.

5146.belief: There is one particular way to present art research and it has to look polished.
5146.statement: There is one particular way to present art research and it has to look polished.
5146.correction: Artist research should be meaningful, it may look polished, but it may also just look purposeful and be presented with care.

1908.correction: A concept can develop and evolve but it should not completely change without very good reason.

2987.belief: A final piece must be large scale and completely finished.
2987.statement: A final piece must be large scale and completely finished.
2987.correction: A final piece or outcome is just the end point in your journey so far, it should resolve your ideas but it can do this in many ways and in different scales.

5716.belief: Portraits are just about what someone looks like on the surface with no deeper meaning.
5716.statement: Portraits are just about what someone looks like on the surface with no deeper meaning.
5716.correction: While capturing someone’s physical appearance can be part of a portrait, photographers often go much deeper. Portraits can reveal who someone is, exploring culture, identity, relationships, life experiences and even social or political themes.

5056.belief: Objects in photography are only depicted realistically.
5056.statement: Objects in photography are only depicted realistically.
5056.correction: Objects can be used in a range of ways in photography. Objects in photography can be used as a subject that might also contain symbolic meanings.

4832.belief: Natural forms are always perfectly symmetrical, like leaves or flowers.
4832.statement: Natural forms are always perfectly symmetrical, like leaves or flowers.
4832.correction: While some natural forms show symmetry, most have irregular, flowing shapes. Even symmetrical forms often have variations, this is part of what makes nature interesting to photographers.

4016.belief: Landscapes are just pretty pictures of nature – there's not much meaning behind them.
4016.statement: Landscapes are just pretty pictures of nature – there's not much meaning behind them.
4016.correction: While landscapes often show beautiful scenery, they can express powerful ideas, like climate change, migration, culture, or even identity. Photographers use landscapes not just to show what they see, but to say something about how they feel or value.

4145.belief: Light and dark are only used to make things look realistic, not to create mood.
4145.statement: Light and dark are only used to make things look realistic, not to create mood.
4145.correction: This overlooks how artists intentionally use contrast to suggest emotion, tension, calm, or drama, not just realism.

3805.belief: "Inside" and "outside" in design always refers to physical spaces, like buildings or rooms.
3805.statement: "Inside" and "outside" in design always refers to physical spaces, like buildings or rooms.
3805.correction: In design, "inside" and "outside" can mean more than places — they can show how someone feels on the inside, how people hide emotions, or the contrast between personal and public life.

5717.belief: Portraits are just about what someone looks like - they’re mainly about getting the likeness right.
5717.statement: Portraits are just about what someone looks like - they’re mainly about getting the likeness right.
5717.correction: While capturing someone’s physical appearance can be part of a portrait, artists often go much deeper. Portraits can reveal who someone is, exploring culture, identity, relationships, life experiences and even social or political themes.

5050.belief: Objects in art are only depicted in realistic pictures.
5050.statement: Objects in art are only depicted in realistic pictures.
5050.correction: Objects can be used in a range of ways in art. Objects can be used as a textile art material or as the subject of an artwork. Objects in art often contain symbolic meanings.

3804.belief: "Inside" and "outside" in art always refers to physical spaces, like buildings or rooms.
3804.statement: "Inside" and "outside" in art always refers to physical spaces, like buildings or rooms.
3804.correction: In art, "inside" and "outside" can mean more than places — they can show how someone feels on the inside, how people hide emotions, or the contrast between personal and public life.

9143.belief: All sculptures of people are just made to look realistic or beautiful.
9143.statement: All sculptures of people are just made to look realistic or beautiful.
9143.correction: Artists often use figures to tell stories, express ideas, or explore identity, emotions, or social issues. A figure might be exaggerated, abstract, or symbolic to make people think or feel something.

32.belief: 3D design is only about how things look.
32.statement: 3D design is only about how things look.
32.correction: While appearance (aesthetics) is important, 3D design also prioritises function, usability and interaction with real space. Especially in product and furniture design, how an object works is just as critical as how it looks.

4833.belief: Natural forms are just used to make things look pretty; they don’t have real purpose in design.
4833.statement: Natural forms are just used to make things look pretty; they don’t have real purpose in design.
4833.correction: Natural forms can inspire smart, efficient and eco-friendly designs through biomimicry. For example, the form of a bird’s wing has influenced airplane design. Artists can use natural forms to solve problems and raise awareness about the environment.

362.belief: Architecture is just about making buildings look nice, not about solving problems or reflecting culture.
362.statement: Architecture is just about making buildings look nice, not about solving problems or reflecting culture.
362.correction: Architecture is about much more than appearance. It solves practical problems like shelter and space, and reflects cultural values, history, and how people live.

4143.belief: Light in 3D design is only functional, used just to illuminate an object.
4143.statement: Light in 3D design is only functional, used just to illuminate an object.
4143.correction: While light can serve a practical purpose, in 3D design it is also a creative tool. It influences mood, draws attention to key areas and enhances the way forms and textures are perceived. Light can be as expressive as colour or shape.

31.belief: 3D design is just about making things look good, it doesn't need to express deeper ideas.
31.statement: 3D design is just about making things look good, it doesn't need to express deeper ideas.
31.correction: While aesthetics are important, 3D design is also a powerful way to communicate ideas and solve problems. It can explore complex themes through physical form, material choice, and spatial design. Good design combines purpose with meaning.

5715.belief: Portraits are just about what someone looks like and mainly focus on capturing a likeness.
5715.statement: Portraits are just about what someone looks like and mainly focus on capturing a likeness.
5715.correction: While capturing someone’s physical appearance can be part of a portrait, artists often go much deeper. Portraits can reveal who someone is, exploring culture, identity, relationships, life experiences and even social or political themes.

9284.belief: Silhouette just means a shadow or outline — it doesn’t really matter in textile design.
9284.statement: Silhouette just means a shadow or outline — it doesn’t really matter in textile design.
9284.correction: Silhouette is essential in textiles — it defines shape, structure and how a garment or piece interacts with light and contrast. Designers use silhouettes to make bold visual statements, create mood and control how the textile is seen in space.

3806.belief: Inside and outside just means indoors and outdoors.
3806.statement: Inside and outside just means indoors and outdoors.
3806.correction: Inside and outside can also mean emotional states, identity, or private vs public. Artists use space, scale, and materials to explore physical and psychological boundaries.

5713.belief: Portraits in graphic design must look realistic to be effective.
5713.statement: Portraits in graphic design must look realistic to be effective.
5713.correction: Graphic design often relies on abstraction and stylisation to communicate more clearly and powerfully than realism - effective portraits use design choices to enhance meaning, not replicate reality.

3375.belief: Graphic design is only done on computers and doesn’t involve drawing or observational skills.
3375.statement: Graphic design is only done on computers and doesn’t involve drawing or observational skills.
3375.correction: Graphic design often begins with hand-drawn ideas, including observational drawing. Understanding shape, form, and composition from real objects improves digital outcomes.

3377.belief: Graphic design is mostly digital, so nature isn’t really relevant.
3377.statement: Graphic design is mostly digital, so nature isn’t really relevant.
3377.correction: Graphic design often draws from organic, natural inspiration - many professional designs use textures, forms, and concepts from nature to create emotional or symbolic meaning.

3376.belief: Graphic design landscapes must look realistic to be effective.
3376.statement: Graphic design landscapes must look realistic to be effective.
3376.correction: In graphic communication, the goal is to communicate visually, not replicate reality. Stylised or abstracted landscapes can be more impactful and expressive.

432.belief: All artists take inspiration from one source.
432.statement: All artists take inspiration from one source.
432.correction: Artists might take inspiration from a wide range of sources including surroundings, objects, personal experiences, memories, artist's work or historical and contemporary movements.

4913.belief: Negative life experiences cannot be used as inspiration for creating artwork.
4913.statement: Negative life experiences cannot be used as inspiration for creating artwork.
4913.correction: Many artists find that exploring difficult life experiences can lead to meaningful creative work.

314.belief: Annotation has to be long, written paragraphs.
314.statement: Annotation has to be long, written paragraphs.
314.correction: Annotation can be short notes, labels, sketches, diagrams, or even audio recordings. It’s any way you add extra information to explain your ideas clearly.

398.belief: Art materials don’t matter beyond how they look or feel.
398.statement: Art materials don’t matter beyond how they look or feel.
398.correction: Materials can carry deep personal and cultural meanings that add important layers to the artwork’s story and message.

4481.belief: The material an artist uses doesn’t matter as long as the subject or idea is strong.
4481.statement: The material an artist uses doesn’t matter as long as the subject or idea is strong.
4481.correction: The choice of materials greatly affects how an artwork looks, feels and communicates meaning. Materials can add texture, symbolism and emotional impact that deepen the viewer’s understanding.

538.belief: Balance means everything must be perfectly symmetrical.
538.statement: Balance means everything must be perfectly symmetrical.
538.correction: Balance can be symmetrical, but it can also be asymmetrical or radial. Asymmetrical balance uses different elements on each side to create visual stability.

1796.belief: A common misconception about paint pouring is that it’s purely random and anyone can do it without skill.
1796.statement: A common misconception about paint pouring is that it’s purely random and anyone can do it without skill.
1796.correction: In reality, while paint pouring involves chance, artists use technique, colour theory and control to create intentional and successful compositions. It’s both creative and technical.

3025.belief: First-hand observations have to be drawings.
3025.statement: First-hand observations have to be drawings
3025.correction: First-hand observations can also include photography, sound recordings, writing, collected objects, or video — any direct response to real-life experiences.

1794.belief: A common misconception about this lesson is that photography is just about capturing what you see, when in fact it involves making creative choices.
1794.statement: A common misconception about this lesson is that photography is just about capturing what you see, when in fact it involves making creative choices.
1794.correction: Photography is about deciding how to show the subject to communicate an idea or feeling. Understanding that really opens up creative possibilities.

5094.belief: Once a photo or drawing is finished, it can’t be changed or developed further.
5094.statement: Once a photo or drawing is finished, it can’t be changed or developed further.
5094.correction: A finished photo or drawing is just a starting point—artists often rework, edit, layer, or translate their images into new forms using different media to explore deeper meaning or fresh creative directions.

5311.belief: Only paper and canvas are proper or professional surfaces for making art.
5311.statement: Only paper and canvas are proper or professional surfaces for making art
5311.correction: Artists have long worked on a wide range of surfaces, including wood, metal, glass, fabric, cardboard, plastic, ceramics, and more. The surface is a creative choice, not a limitation.

2478.belief: If you don’t use traditional art materials, your work won’t be taken seriously or get a high grade.
2478.statement: If you don’t use traditional art materials, your work won’t be taken seriously or get a high grade.
2478.correction: Art & Design encourages experimentation with a wide range of materials — not just pencil, paint and clay. Using unusual or personal materials can strengthen marks if they are purposeful, linked to ideas and part of a thoughtful process.

2303.belief: More detail always makes an artwork better.
2303.statement: More detail always makes an artwork better.
2303.correction: Too much detail—especially if it’s unfocused—can make an artwork feel cluttered, overwhelming, or take attention away from the focal point.

1800.belief: A common misconception about technical aspects in art is that technical skill only means making artworks look realistic.
1800.statement: A common misconception about technical aspects in art is that technical skill only means making artworks look realistic.
1800.correction: Technical skill also includes mastery of materials, control of techniques and the ability to use those skills effectively in any style, whether abstract, expressive, or conceptual.

1798.belief: A common misconception about portfolios is that you need to include everything you've made.
1798.statement: A common misconception about portfolios is that you need to include everything you've made.
1798.correction: It's much better to select work that clearly shows your ideas, development, artistic journey and skills.

3341.belief: A good portfolio presentation should be is highly decorative and colourful to be engaging.
3341.statement: A good portfolio presentation should be is highly decorative and colourful to be engaging.
3341.correction: While creative touches like washi tape or coloured paint can add personality, a clean and minimal layout can be just as effective, sometimes even more so. The goal is to curate a cohesive presentation that supports your work, not distracts from it

2854.belief: Expensive or professional materials automatically produce better artwork.
2854.statement: Expensive or professional materials automatically produce better artwork.
2854.correction: The quality of the outcome depends more on how materials are used, combined, and manipulated, rather than their cost or brand.

8826.belief: Reflection is only about finding faults or criticising your work.
8826.statement: Reflection is only about finding faults or criticising your work.
8826.correction: Reflection is about recognising both strengths and areas to improve in order to grow as an artist.

1790.belief: A common misconception about collaboration is that everyone has to agree on every detail or work in the same style for it to succeed.
1790.statement: A common misconception about collaboration is that everyone has to agree on every detail or work in the same style for it to succeed.
1790.correction: In reality, differing approaches and opinions can make the final artwork more dynamic and original.

2829.belief: Everyone has to work on the same part of the collaborative art piece at the same time.
2829.statement: Everyone has to work on the same part of the collaborative art piece at the same time.
2829.correction: In reality, collaboration can also mean dividing tasks, working on separate elements that are later combined, or contributing in different ways, such as planning, designing, making, or assembling.

8856.belief: Reimagining work means simply copying the original in a slightly different way.
8856.statement: Reimagining work means simply copying the original in a slightly different way.
8856.correction: Reimagining is about transforming the original work, changing materials, scale, techniques, or context to create something new that still connects back to the starting point.

1791.belief: A common misconception about collaborative annotation is that it’s just about leaving individual notes side by side.
1791.statement: A common misconception about collaborative annotation is that it’s just about leaving individual notes side by side.
1791.correction: In reality, the purpose is not only to make comments but to interact with each other's ideas, responding, questioning and building connections so that understanding is developed collectively rather than in isolation.

1752.belief: Collaborative artwork ends when the group finishes working together.
1752.statement: Collaborative artwork ends when the group finishes working together.
1752.correction: In reality, collaborative pieces continue to evolve as viewers engage with them, as participants reflect on the process and as the artwork is displayed or adapted in new contexts.

3581.belief: Every idea must be innovative and interdisciplinary.
3581.statement: Every idea must be innovative and interdisciplinary.
3581.correction: Sometimes taking ideas and inspiration from others or following a tried and tested path moves you forward.

9176.belief: I should select an artist because their work looks like the work I would like to create.
9176.statement: I should select an artist because their work looks like the work I would like to create.
9176.correction: This is one reason, but more in depth critique will help you select artists based on ideas and visual language that can help you make original work that is more personal and meaningful to you.

4372.belief: I can just make lots of different versions and present them as experiments.
4372.statement: I can just make lots of different versions and present them as experiments.
4372.correction: Experimentation is about thinking through doing. It is only useful when it moves your creative journey forward.

2468.belief: You don't need to record failures as it will lower your GCSE grade.
2468.statement: You don't need to record failures as it will lower your GCSE grade.
2468.correction: Record all of your experiments, but make it clear in your work that you know which ones were successful and take these forward in your creative journey. This is evidence of your informed and insightful approach. This will attract a higher mark.

4381.belief: As I have to make something personal I can't copy an artist's ideas or techniques.
4381.statement: As I have to make something personal I can't copy an artist's ideas or techniques.
4381.correction: Copying or pastiche can help you learn techniques, but to create original work that meets the A04 objective, you must also add your own ideas and intentions.

4876.belief: I need new resources for my response.
4876.statement: I need new resources for my response.
4876.correction: You need suitable resources, ideally first-hand. They don't need to be new they can be sourced from bits of your project so far.

1881.belief: Composition is more relevant to 2D work.
1881.statement: Composition is more relevant to 2D work.
1881.correction: Composition is relevant to all areas of art practice as it's about deciding on the best arrangement for your work. It will be dictated by your intentions for the piece. In 3D, we consider the composition from all angles or in the round.

10118.belief: You should take forward all of the suggestions from your critique to improve your response.
10118.statement: You should take forward all of the suggestions from your critique to improve your response.
10118.correction: You should listen to and consider all suggestions carefully, but you are expected to respond in a personal and meaningful way, so trust in your own artistic voice. You should take the suggestions forward if they align with your vision and style.

8923.belief: The response from the timed period is marked as a stand alone outcome.
8923.statement: The response from the timed period is marked as a stand alone outcome.
8923.correction: The marks are awarded holistically and take in the whole creative process. This period is a great way to resolve your ideas and spend time focusing on realising your intentions. It shouldn't be incredibly stressful or worry you!

829.belief: You cannot remove any work from your book or portfolio.
829.statement: You cannot remove any work from your book or portfolio.
829.correction: You should select your work carefully and on rare occasions you might find work that doesn't add to the creative journey and is best left out. Discuss these pieces with your teacher to get guidance first.

10131.belief: I should talk about all of the visual elements and principles of art in my evaluation.
10131.statement: I should talk about all of the visual elements and principles of art in my evaluation.
10131.correction: Select and describe only the areas that are relevant, but consider them all to see if you notice anything new. Sometimes you make work instinctively and don't realise until later what techniques or principles you actually applied.

3409.belief: A group crit is only useful while the project is ongoing.
3409.statement: A group crit is only useful while the project is ongoing.
3409.correction: A group crit involves diverse perspectives. Even if you don’t incorporate it into your current work, it helps you understand different viewpoints to improve your skills and help you anticipate opinions in future projects, making you a better artist.

10951.belief: The way you show your work doesn't really matter so long as it's tidy.
10951.statement: The way you show your work doesn't really matter so long as it's tidy.
10951.correction: A creative, careful presentation will support the idea, message or mood and help make your work impactful.

2626.belief: The elements and principles of art are the same thing.
2626.statement: The elements and principles of art are the same thing.
2626.correction: Remind pupils that the core principles are: balance, movement, rhythm, pattern, contrast, unity, emphasis. The elements are the components that artists use to create an artwork.

7677.belief: Only brushes are used in painting.
7677.statement: Pupils may think that only brushes are used in painting.
7677.correction: Through modelling and explanation - remind pupils that there are a range of painting tools and materials that can be used to apply paint to a surface.

8300.belief: Any surface works the same and that there is one correct tool for painting.
8300.statement: Pupils may think any surface works the same and that there is one correct tool for painting.
8300.correction: There’s no single “right” tool. Brushes give precision, while palette knives, sponges, or fingers add texture. The surface also matters. Paper absorbs, primed canvas holds paint, and board gives smooth results.

7713.statement: Pupils may think that colour has universal meanings.
7713.correction: Remind pupils that colour has different symbolic meaning around the world.

10937.belief: Watercolours are opaque and used for solid blocks of colour.
10937.statement: Watercolours are opaque and used for solid blocks of colour.
10937.correction: Watercolours are actually transparent and unpredictable, with the paper providing the lightest value.

898.belief: Centering the subject is always best.
898.statement: Centering the subject is always best.
898.correction: Placing the focal point dead centre can make the painting feel static or dull. Using the Rule of Thirds or Golden Ratio often creates more dynamic, engaging compositions.

4055.belief: More layers is equal to a better painting.
4055.statement: More layers is equal to a better painting.
4055.correction: Quantity doesn’t guarantee quality. Effective layering is about intentionality, each layer should serve a purpose, whether it’s adjusting tone, adding texture, or enhancing light.

5814.belief: Printing is only about copying or replicating an image.
5814.statement: Printing is only about copying or replicating an image.
5814.correction: Printing is a creative process where choices about technique, layering, and texture produce unique outcomes - even when using the same plate or block.

3797.belief: More ink always produces stronger, better prints.
3797.statement: More ink always produces stronger, better prints.
3797.correction: Too much ink causes smudging and loss of detail; even, thin layers produce cleaner and sharper results.

3796.belief: The ink should be applied only to the raised surface of the plate.
3796.statement: The ink should be applied only to the raised surface of the plate.
3796.correction: In intaglio printing, the recessed lines hold the ink - the surface must be wiped clean so only incised marks transfer ink to paper.

3451.belief: The harder you push the squeegee, the better the print.
3451.statement: The harder you push the squeegee, the better the print.
3451.correction: Too much pressure forces excess ink and blurs edges - controlled, even pressure produces the sharpest results.

3621.belief: Any image from the internet will print clearly at large scale.
3621.statement: Any image from the internet will print clearly at large scale.
3621.correction: Resolution and image type matter - a raster image may pixelate when enlarged, while vector graphics remain sharp.

2385.correction: Digital tools enhance traditional methods by expanding creative possibilities - neither replaces the other.

4716.belief: Monoprints should look “perfect” and repeatable, like digital prints.
4716.statement: Monoprints should look “perfect” and repeatable, like digital prints.
4716.correction: Monoprints are valued for their unique, imperfect, and expressive qualities that cannot be exactly replicated.

3486.belief: Higher resolution always makes digital artwork better.
3486.statement: Higher resolution always makes digital artwork better.
3486.correction: Higher resolution increases detail but may not improve design choices; strong composition and contrast matter more for impact.

309.belief: Animation is just drawing moving pictures quickly.
309.statement: Animation is just drawing moving pictures quickly.
309.correction: Animation is carefully planned, using frames, keyframes, and digital tools to control timing, pace, and movement.

2370.belief: Digital art lacks the creativity or authenticity of traditional methods.
2370.statement: Digital art lacks the creativity or authenticity of traditional methods.
2370.correction: Digital tools expand, rather than replace, creativity. Artists can blend hand-drawn, painted, or textured work into digital layers to achieve unique results.

2150.belief: Cyanotype images always appear instantly after sun exposure.
2150.statement: Cyanotype images always appear instantly after sun exposure.
2150.correction: The image develops gradually and deepens in colour after rinsing and drying; exposure time and sunlight intensity affect results.

5493.belief: Photo manipulation is just applying filters.
5493.statement: Photo manipulation is just applying filters.
5493.correction: Filters are quick presets, but artful digital manipulation involves purposeful use of tools (layers, selections, cloning, adjustments) to control outcome and meaning.

10383.belief: Transforming an image always means stretching or resizing it.
10383.statement: Transforming an image always means stretching or resizing it.
10383.correction: Transformation in digital art includes combining, masking, blending, and reimagining images - not just changing size or shape.

10695.belief: Using digital brushes automatically makes artwork look realistic.
10695.statement: Using digital brushes automatically makes artwork look realistic.
10695.correction: Realism depends on how brush settings, layering and blending are applied - not the tool itself. Technique and practice are crucial.

10637.belief: If I use the same motif, my work will always look the same.
10637.statement: If I use the same motif, my work will always look the same.
10637.correction: Using different techniques can change your textile work. A motif may look flat when printed, detailed with embroidery, or bold and layered in appliqué. Your choice of textile technique changes the way a motif is interpreted.

9620.belief: Stitching is for securing fabric pieces together so the type of stitch should be uniform.
9620.statement: Stitching is for securing fabric pieces together so the type of stitch should be uniform.
9620.correction: Using a variety of embroidery stitches when creating a refined sample creates visual interest, contrast, texture and depth to the design.

2528.belief: All dyeing methods colour fabric evenly across the whole surface.
2528.statement: All dyeing methods colour fabric evenly across the whole surface.
2528.correction: Different dyeing methods produce different effects, techniques like dip-dyeing, tie-dye, or resist create uneven or patterned results, while immersion dyeing can give a more uniform colour.

2885.belief: Fabric manipulation is only used to make clothes look more decorative.
2885.statement: Fabric manipulation is only used to make clothes look more decorative.
2885.correction: Fabric manipulation does add decoration, but it can also change the structure of fabric. Techniques like ruching, folding, or layering can give garments shape, volume, and movement, not just surface detail.

1999.belief: Constructed textiles are only made by weaving on a loom.
1999.statement: Constructed textiles are only made by weaving on a loom.
1999.correction: Constructed textiles include any fabric created by interlacing, knotting, looping, or bonding fibres such as weaving, knitting, crochet, macramé and even non-woven techniques, not just loom weaving.

10220.belief: Thematic development means I have to use as many different ideas as possible to make my work interesting.
10220.statement: Thematic development means I have to use as many different ideas as possible to make my work interesting.
10220.correction: Actually, thematic development is about refining ideas so your motifs and techniques feel connected. Too many unrelated ideas can make a design look chaotic — repeating and varying motifs from one clear theme helps create cohesion.

2461.belief: You don't need drawings in a textile project.
2461.statement: You don't need drawings in a textile project.
2461.correction: Drawing motifs and sketching developmental ideas during the initial stages in design work helps to consolidate ideas.

9140.belief: Sculpture is only about the outside shape.
9140.statement: Sculpture is only about the outside shape.
9140.correction: Sculpture also uses negative space, scale and proportion to create meaning and viewer impact.

459.belief: Assemblage is just sticking things together randomly.
459.statement: Assemblage is just sticking things together randomly.
459.correction: Assemblage is not random; artists carefully plan how objects interact. Each choice affects rhythm, meaning, balance and stability.

872.belief: Carving is just about 'chipping away' randomly until a shape appears.
872.statement: Carving is just about 'chipping away' randomly until a shape appears.
872.correction: Skilled carving is deliberate - starting with planning, respecting grain, and refining in controlled stages.

1645.belief: Choosing intresting materials or shapes is enough to make a sculpture 'meaningful'.
1645.statement: Choosing intresting materials or shapes is enough to make a sculpture 'meaningful'.
1645.correction: A sculpture is powerful when choices are intentional. Materials, forms, and symbols must link clearly to a theme; without this, the work can feel random instead of meaningful.

881.belief: All casts look the same no matter what material is used.
881.statement: All casts look the same no matter what material is used.
881.correction: Different materials give different textures, weights, weights and finishes - same mould different outcomes.

4669.belief: Mixed media just means throwing lots of materials together.
4669.statement: Mixed media just means throwing lots of materials together.
4669.correction: Each material should have a purpose — it must add meaning or structure, not just make it look busy.

1696.belief: Clay Sculptures are finished once the shape is made.
1696.statement: Clay Sculptures are finished once the shape is made.
1696.correction: Clay work is a process; refinment, moisture control and surface texture are key to a finished sculpture.

2378.belief: Digital drawing doesn’t require the same skills as traditional drawing.
2378.statement: Digital drawing doesn’t require the same skills as traditional drawing.
2378.correction: Core artistic skills like proportion, tone and composition still apply in digital artworks. Digital tools simply offer new ways to achieve them.

815.belief: Any camera setting will capture light drawings.
815.statement: Any camera setting will capture light drawings.
815.correction: Long exposure (slow shutter speed) is essential for creating light drawings, without it, the camera won’t capture light movement, only still images.

33.belief: 3D drawings must look exactly like 2D sketches.
33.statement: 3D drawings must look exactly like 2D sketches.
33.correction: 3D drawing explores form and space - it’s about expressing line, contour and movement in three dimensions, not replicating flat sketches.

4386.belief: Making an exhibition is just about hanging art.
4386.statement: Making an exhibition is just about hanging art.
4386.correction: Curation requires skills and knowledge. Curation can create connections and a narrative between individual works.

5841.belief: Only professional curators decide what is exhibited.
5841.statement: Only professional curators decide what is exhibited.
5841.correction: Throughout history and globally, artists have curated their own work. Sometimes artists self-curate but sometimes this process can be in collaboration with professional curators.

10161.belief: The most technically perfect pieces should always be selected for exhibitions.
10161.statement: The most technically perfect pieces should always be selected for exhibitions.
10161.correction: An exhibition’s power lies in how the works connect thematically, emotionally, and conceptually, not only in technical skill.

5787.correction: Presentation is part of communication, not decoration.

8900.belief: Reproduction is only possible with a photocopier/printer and reproductions are not as valid as originals.
8900.statement: Reproduction is only possible with a photocopier/printer and reproductions are not as valid as originals.
8900.correction: Hand-made reproductions (drawn, traced, collaged, reinterpreted) are also valid artistic processes.

410.belief: An artist statement has to be a long, formal piece of writing full of complicated words.
410.statement: An artist statement has to be a long, formal piece of writing full of complicated words.
410.correction: Artist statements can be short and simple, written in clear and honest language, and can also take other formats such as bullet points, spoken word, visual mind maps, captions, or short videos.

434.belief: Artists only talk about their work to promote it in galleries and museums.
434.statement: Artists only talk about their work to promote it in galleries and museums.
434.correction: Artists might talk about their work for engagement and promotion, in a variety of contexts.

5861.belief: Promoting a show is just about putting up a poster or posting once online.
5861.statement: Promoting a show is just about putting up a poster or posting once online.
5861.correction: Effective promotion requires planning, multiple methods, and consistent communication.
